issues.legal_issue: A ruler may lose sovereignty through a gradual historical process of submission, even without conquest or an express agreement imposing the successor ruler’s sovereignty.
material_facts: The former rulers of the territories had submitted to the ruler of a larger state over a continuous process, although there was no evidence of conquest or an express agreement imposing sovereignty.
The larger state’s laws applied in the territories by their own force, and its ruler’s staff exercised administrative control there.
By the time the larger state merged with the successor state, the former rulers exercised no remaining sovereign authority.
issues.conclusion: The former rulers had ceased to be sovereign before the merger and were subjects of the larger state’s ruler.
issues.legal_principle: An assumption of sovereign powers may occur by conquest, treaty, cession, or otherwise, and may result from a historical process over many years; sovereignty may pass without the territory itself merging into the new state. The Court applied Promod Chandra Deb v. State of Orissa, [1962] Supp. 1 S.C.R. 405, and referred to the analogous situations in Thakur Amar Singhji v. State of Rajasthan, [1955] 2 S.C.R. 303, and Amarsarjit Singh v. State of Punjab, [1962] Supp. 3 S.C.R. 346.

rule.if: land_acquisition_appeal and gradual_submission and successor_laws_applied and successor_admin_control

predicates.land_acquisition_appeal: An appeal challenged the state’s acquisition of land held by former local rulers.
predicates.gradual_submission: Former local rulers submitted to a superior ruler through conduct over a period of time.
predicates.successor_laws_applied: The superior ruler’s laws operated in the territories by their own force.
predicates.successor_admin_control: The superior ruler’s staff exercised administrative control over the territories.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenging land acquisition concerns territories where former rulers gradually submitted to a superior ruler and that ruler’s laws and administration operated, the former rulers lacked sovereignty at integration.

issues.legal_issue: A non-sovereign holder of an interest in land between cultivators and the state is an intermediary, and that interest may be acquired when it falls within the statutory definition of an estate.
material_facts: After the merger, the former rulers were not sovereigns and held interests in land between the cultivators and the state.
They were not cultivators and had paid takoli to the ruler of the larger state and later to the successor state; the Court treated those payments as land revenue.
The amended definitions covered holders or owners of interests in land between the cultivator and the state and included qualifying lands and interests held by an intermediary.
issues.conclusion: The former rulers were intermediaries, their lands were estates under the amended definitions, and their interests in those lands could be acquired under the Act.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 2(h) and 2(g) of the Orissa Estates Abolition Act, 1952, as amended by the Orissa Estates Abolition (Amendment) Act, 1954, define an intermediary to include other holders or owners of interests in land between the raiyat and the state, and define an estate to include qualifying land held by or vested in an intermediary. Explanations I and III to section 2(g) address land revenue and estates in merged territories. The Court also noted its earlier decision in Biswambhar Singh v. State of Orissa, [1954] S.C.R. 842, which had held that these proprietors were not intermediaries under the earlier definition.

rule.if: land_acquisition_appeal and holders_lacked_sovereignty and holders_not_cultivators and land_interest_between_cultivators_and_state and land_payments_made_to_ruler

predicates.land_acquisition_appeal: An appeal challenged the state’s acquisition of land held by former local rulers.
predicates.holders_lacked_sovereignty: The holders had no sovereign authority when the relevant territories became part of the successor state.
predicates.holders_not_cultivators: The holders did not occupy the land as cultivators.
predicates.land_interest_between_cultivators_and_st: The holders owned or held an interest in land between the cultivators and the state.
predicates.land_payments_made_to_ruler: The holders made payments relating to the land to the superior ruler or the successor state.

issues.definition: When an acquisition appeal concerns non-sovereign, non-cultivating holders whose land interests lie between cultivators and the state and who made land-related payments to the ruler, those interests are acquirable as estates.
